metadata.title: Assessing the Irritation and Sensitization Potential of Transdermal and Topical Delivery Systems for ANDAs: Draft Guidance for Industry

candidates.statement: The components and composition of a TDS formulation, including the nature of the drug 53 substance and/or the degree to which the TDS materials occlude the transmission of water vapor 54 from the skin, in conjunction with other factors such as the environmental humidity or the 55 condition of the skin, may have the potential to irritate the skin or lead to a sensitization 56 reaction. 7 Such reactions can be unpleasant to the patient and may affect patient compliance, 57 skin permeability, and/or adhesion of the TDS to the skin. The collective consequence of these 58 potential effects could create uncertainty about the resulting drug delivery profile and the rate 59 and extent of drug absorption from the TDS. Therefore, when appropriate, applicants should 60 perform a comparative assessment of the T and R TDS products using an appropriately designed 61 skin irritation study or combined skin irritation and sensitization study with human subjects to 62

candidates.statement: Changes in environmental temperature or humidity, including the daily exposure of the TDS to 76 heat and water during routine showering, may transiently affect the rate at which components of 77 the TDS formulation are released and permeate through skin. Such changes may also affect 78 entrapped moisture in and/or under the TDS, which could alter skin hydration and impact the 79 bioavailability of formulation components, which may, in turn, change irritation and/or 80 sensitization reactions. Therefore, applicants should consider any conditions of labeled use for 81 the RLD that may impact the irritation or sensitization potential of a TDS product (e.g., 82 incidental exposure of the TDS to water, such as while bathing or showering, particularly for a 83 TDS with a duration of wear that is up to or greater than 24 hours). 84

candidates.statement: In addition to irritation and sensitization reactions that may arise from the corrosive or 86 immunomodulatory nature of formulation components or from the pharmacodynamic response 87 of the skin to the occlusion by the TDS, the skin may also become irritated in response to the 88 physical insults that can occur during the removal of a TDS. For example, if the adhesive 89 properties of the TDS are such that it strips away substantial portions of the stratum corneum 90 during removal, the damage to the skin barrier may lead to irritation at the site of TDS removal. 91 Accordingly, applicants should also consider the adhesive components of the TDS and physical 92 insults from removal of the TDS that may impact the irritation potential of a TDS product. 93

candidates.statement: In general, the Agency recommends that applicants conduct an evaluator-blinded, randomized 112 study to support their comparative evaluation of the skin irritation characteristics of the T and R 113 products. The study population should typically include healthy males and nonpregnant, 114 nonlactating females, unless product-specific considerations consistent with the RLD’s labeled 115 conditions of use for certain TDS products indicate otherwise. 10 In the study protocol, the choice 116 of TDS strength intended to be used should be prespecified and should be justified, as 117 appropriate, based upon the use of the TDS in the proposed study population. When evaluating 118 the irritation potential only, applicants should compare the T and R TDS products in a minimum 119 of 40 evaluable subjects, or a sufficient number of subjects to power the study at a level of 0.80 120 or higher, whichever sample size is greater. To evaluate the irritation potential only, the study 121 should consist of a single 21-day induction phase under provocative conditions (repeated 122 removal and reapplication of the TDS on the same skin site) to maximize the potential for the 123 occurrence of an irritation in accordance with the recommendations described below. 124

candidates.context: 2. Study Conduct Considerations 188 A trained observer should score the TDS’s adherence and the subject’s skin reactions at each 194 TDS removal, and applicants should try to ensure that the same scorer is used for all 195 observations. If the same scorer is not used for all observations, applicants should provide 196 evidence to ensure that the scoring is consistent across different scorers. Because of likely 197 differences in the appearance of the TDS between the T product and the R product, blinding of 198 the observer may not be possible, especially for monitoring TDS adhesion, which requires direct 199 observation of the TDS. However, applicants should try to blind the evaluation of irritation and 200 sensitization when possible. 201

candidates.statement: FDA’s recommended primary endpoint for evaluating irritation is the mean irritation score 329 (MIS). At each assessment time point for each subject and for each product, applicants should 330 calculate a combined irritation score by adding the “dermal response” score and the numeric 331 equivalent for “other effects” letter score. For each subject and each product, applicants should 332 calculate the MIS as the sum of the combined irritation scores over the assessment time points 333 divided by the total number of assessments.
